zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

美國職缺大增，使週二美債漲勢收斂。長天期公債收復部分週一跌幅，2年期殖利率卻未下降。10年期殖利率跌1個基點至4.46%，30年期跌2個基點至4.97%；勞動市場有韌性，聯準會又持續關切通膨，讓前端殖利率維持4.05%。

4月職缺升至762萬個，為近兩年最高，裁員也減少。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack表示，不確定性下維持利率仍屬合理，但價格壓力若持續，可能很快需要行動。交換市場反映12月前約18個基點的緊縮幅度。油價在週一區間內小幅上漲，沒有明顯改變這項政策展望。

信用債買家較不猶豫。Blue Owl Technology Finance及一座與CoreWeave有關的資料中心，都擴大售債並取得優於初步討論的價格。半導體股大漲5.87%，風險資產與長期美債同步走高。海外方面，日本標售強勁，英國公債的高殖利率也吸引買盤，在央行緊縮預期升溫之際，為債市提供支撐。

## 職缺數據使美債漲勢收斂

職位空缺及勞動力流動調查（JOLTS）公布前，美國公債一度接近一個月來最佳價位。4月職缺由3月的689萬個升至762萬個，大幅高於預期中位數687萬個，裁員減少也顯示勞動市場正在穩定。其他細節仍有好有壞，未引發新一波拋售，但報告降低了寬鬆急迫性，殖利率因此離開低點。

Hammack認為就業已接近充分就業，現行政策利率未必具有限制性。商品與非住宅服務價格普遍承壓，加上4月PCE年增率達3.8%，使她保持謹慎。等待不代表排除升息；交換市場反映12月前約18個基點的緊縮，並完全反映2027年3月前升息0.25個百分點。

殖利率曲線呈現這項差異。2年期維持4.05%，5年期下降1個基點至4.17%，10年期下降1個基點至4.46%，30年期下降2個基點至4.97%。2s10s利差收窄1個基點至41個基點，2s30s收窄2個基點至92個基點；2s5s10s蝶式利差下降1個基點至負17個基點，2s10s30s維持負10個基點。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.39%，解釋了名目殖利率的降幅，實質殖利率則維持2.07%。更長天期實質殖利率也下降，20年期跌1個基點至2.48%，30年期跌2個基點至2.69%；5年期反而升1個基點至1.65%，靠近政策路徑的天期仍承受壓力。

WTI上漲1.74%至$93.76，Brent上漲1.07%至$96.00，都未突破週一交易區間。兩者一個月跌幅分別約8.0%與11.3%，能源衝擊已不如高峰時嚴重，但價格仍高。油價從5月高點回落，先前已協助各天期美債殖利率下降約10至20個基點；週二的小幅變動，反映市場仍在油價緩解與穩健勞動需求之間權衡。

部位也沒有帶來明確方向。交易員已減少部分極端空頭曝險，調查卻顯示投資人從小幅淨多頭回到中性，選擇權交易同時對上漲與下跌避險。接下來的服務業與就業數據，仍有很大機會打破這個平衡。

短期融資維持有序。美國財政部接受約$750億42天期國庫券投標，最高得標利率3.625%，投標倍數由前次2.71倍提高至3.28倍。間接投標者取得獲接受競爭性投標的63.61%，直接投標者占3.62%，交易商占32.77%。這批規模較小的六週券將於6月4日交割。由於沒有發行前交易殖利率可供比較，投標倍數改善及配售結果，是較清楚的需求依據。

國庫券收盤殖利率的變動有限。4週與8週券附息等值殖利率各降1個基點至3.69%與3.70%，6週券升1個基點至3.70%；13週與17週維持3.71%及3.74%，26週與52週則各降1個基點。政策定價仍偏緊，但未見各天期共同反映現金吃緊。

聯準會資產配置則涉及較長期的供給問題。經濟學家Christina Romer與David Romer認為，大幅縮減$6.7兆資產負債表，將帶來重大成本，卻沒有實質好處；有限調整仍可能通過成本效益檢驗。資產中近$4.5兆為美國公債，近$2兆為房貸抵押證券。他們認為MBS集中部位較難合理化，但依2024年以來的自然到期縮減速度，估計仍需超過十年才能處理。若主席Kevin Warsh加快縮減，將影響準備金、房貸債券供給，以及私人投資人需要承接的利率風險。

股市隨債券回升，S&P 500上漲0.13%、Nasdaq 100上漲0.48%、半導體指數上漲5.87%，VIX下降1.74%至15.77%。AI帶動的漲勢，使未來資本支出與發債需求持續受到關注，但當日美債仍主要由能源與聯準會預期主導。美元指數微升0.02%至99.22，黃金上漲0.31%至$4,489.10；外部借款人未承受明顯新增美元壓力，地緣政治避險需求則仍在。

## 信用債買家支持再融資與合約收入

Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp.原先計畫發行$3億，最終提高至$5億，利差為美國公債加265個基點，低於初步討論的約300個基點。這家私人信貸業務發展公司的債券，預期獲惠譽BBB-評等，款項指定用於償還既有債務。

該基金前一季資產價值已下調約5%，Blue Owl也對軟體業貸款變得更謹慎，但基金維持股利不變。即使有這些資產疑慮，投資人仍願意在投資等級最低一級的條件下提供再融資，延續前一交易日業務發展公司仍能取得資金的情況。

瑞銀發行$15億美元AT1資本工具，殖利率6.875%。價格指引最初約7.5%，之後收窄至7.25%至7.375%，首次可贖回時間在2032年底。這是瑞士暫停修改與票息支付能力及替換有關的規則後，瑞銀首次出售AT1。監管不確定性減少有利需求，但較長贖回期及次順位結構，仍使投資人承擔展期與吸收損失的風險。

Elk Grove Village Property完成週一開始銷售的資料中心融資。這家Prime Data Centers間接子公司增發$5,000萬至$9億，5年期債券以面額發行，殖利率7.5%，落在討論區間下緣。芝加哥地區的設施全數租給CoreWeave，租期15年、合約收入約$22億。長約支持銷售，工程、單一承租人，以及對手方的非投資等級信用，仍是風險核心。

資料中心企業今年透過風險較高債券已籌資逾$270億，科技公司整體售債則超過$3,000億。交易順利完成，顯示買家會區分融資架構；規模擴大仍意味私人借款將逐漸與主權債競逐資金。

上市信用債基金大致持平，LQD微跌0.01%，HYG升0.08%，JNK升0.04%。相較這些有限波動，再融資、銀行資本與新基礎設施債務的活動更為明顯。

南韓企業透過改變天期控制成本。截至4月，短期債券與商業本票發行達₩741.4兆，較去年增加47.1%，公司債發行卻下降34.1%。3年期AA無擔保公司債殖利率上升近100個基點至4.4%，3個月商業本票則為3.06%。縮短負債期限可降低當前利息，卻使未來展延融資更容易受到短端利率影響。

美國市政借款人則擴大預付能源融資。California Community Choice Financing Authority核准最多$12.5億債券，為Pioneer Community Energy取得折價長期電力，承銷商為高盛。這類架構由銀行或保險公司收取並投資發債款項，再支付採購能源所需資金；公用事業的能源付款，則支持償付債券。投資人通常可取得高於相同評等市政債的收益。

今年這類交易已發行$146億，較2025年同期增加94%，延續2022年以來每年創紀錄的情況。另一筆Black Belt Energy Gas District的$11.5億預付天然氣債券，預定由美國銀行擔任資金收受方。架構拓寬公共電力事業的融資來源，額外收益背後的風險，仍取決於中介機構信用、能源合約與付款安排。

收購融資也在接近市場。銀行準備提供$25億槓桿貸款與高收益債，再加$2.5億循環額度，支應Long Lake Management以約$63億現金收購American Express Global Business Travel。先前非投資等級併購融資不如預期活躍，市場多為趁需求改善而重訂貸款利差；這筆交易將帶來新的收購槓桿，最終工具分配與定價仍待確定。

英國交易規劃較為平淡。官方數據顯示，第一季完成的國內、外資收購本國企業及本國企業海外收購，合計由495件降至352件，其中外資收購金額從£330億降至£142億。收購減少，可能降低英鎊信用市場的過橋及永久融資需求，與美國活躍的再融資及AI發債形成對照。

## 央行立場偏鷹，高殖利率仍吸引買盤

歐元區5月多項通膨指標加速，整體物價年增率由3.0%升至3.2%，核心達2.5%，服務達3.5%。漲價範圍擴大，強化歐洲央行6月11日升息預期，即使區域商業活動正以2023年以來最快速度萎縮。

Gediminas Simkus主張及時行動，避免通膨加速；Olli Rehn認為預期仍穩定，但同樣需要採取措施。為維護公信力先升息一次，不必然意味長期緊縮循環。不過，若服務價格持續轉嫁，進一步升息的理由便會增強，也會提高投資人持有長債所要求的報酬。

英國央行決策官員Megan Greene表示，伊朗衝突使能源轉嫁延長，近期可能需要升息。貨幣市場完全反映9月前升息0.25個百分點，年底前再升一次的機率為85%。總裁Andrew Bailey則認為仍有一些時間，理由是金融情勢已收緊，需求也脆弱。

高殖利率仍吸引英國公債買家。管理$8,360億資產的Insight Investment，在遠期殖利率來到約6%或更高時，增持較長天期英債。30年期殖利率超過5.5%，在比較的21個已開發市場中最高。這樣的價格可能已提供足夠通膨與財政風險補償，投資人不必先認定英國央行已結束緊縮才願意買入。

日本標售帶來更直接的漲勢。10年期公債投標倍數3.53倍，高於過去12個月平均3.35倍，帶動殖利率下跌11個基點至2.57%。殖利率先前升至1996年以來最高，價格變得有吸引力，長端情緒也改善，買家因此回流。但隔夜指數交換仍反映當月日本央行行動機率約76%，日圓也正逼近每$1兌¥160。

中國央行反而試圖限制殖利率過快下降。在流動性過剩、貸款成長疲弱下，人民銀行僅進行CNY2億7天期逆回購，為歷來最小單日操作。10年期政府債券殖利率週一收於1.70%，創8月以來最低，之後長債期貨回落。低殖利率仍反映中國較弱的成長與信用需求。

美國收盤後的亞洲報導，聚焦油價成本壓力與AI需求同時出現。政府債券殖利率上升，菲律賓披索與印尼盾則因進口帳單及外部收支承壓而走弱。在日本，九名央行委員中，已有五名近期表態支持進一步正常化，總裁植田和男可能取得多數。這些發展增加了下一交易時段面臨的政策問題。

波蘭的通膨結果不同。5月通膨由3.2%降至3.1%，低於預測中位數3.6%，央行因此連續第三個月將主要利率維持3.75%。官員仍列出能源、寬鬆財政、薪資及燃油管制等風險，但實際通膨較低，使波蘭得以暫停行動，與歐元區及英國偏向緊縮的方向不同。

## 財政公信力拉開主權借款人的差距

新興市場美元債上漲，EMB升0.26%，美元大致穩定。整體變動不大，公共財政改善的國家與接近重整的借款人，處境卻相差很遠。

南非截至3月的年度初級盈餘達GDP的1.1%，高於財政部預測0.9%；主要預算赤字4.3%，也優於原估4.6%。官員表示，債務占比在約78.9%達峰後已穩定，預計2033至2034年降至約68.3%。收入改善、支出減少及債務服務成本降低，即使面對共同能源衝擊，仍支持未來信評調升的理由。

塞內加爾的政治衝突使融資困境加深。總統Bassirou Diomaye Faye與總理Ousmane Sonko的內閣爭議，增加財政不確定性。2031年美元債在約54美分交易，低於2月中旬68美分高點，主權利差超過美國公債1,500個基點。該國三檔美元債今年損失2.5%，較廣泛的新興市場美元債指數則上漲1.5%。

投資人預期當月到期的$9,250萬票息會支付，但區域市場另有CFA2,960億、約$5.24億還款，增加現金需求。隱藏負債曝光後，IMF的$18億計畫仍暫停；即使眼前票息支付，也無法解決更大額融資的取得問題。市場對全面重整的預期因而上升。

智利在較穩健的基礎上尋求更多舉債授權。總統Jose Antonio Kast政府要求國會，在原有$174億額度之外再增加$62億，今年已籌資逾$80億。政府將赤字預測從前任的GDP占比1.8%上調至2.4%，並可能發行最多$60億外幣債。

主權殖利率卻小幅下降，違約保護成本降至2月中旬以來最低。市場融資管道仍暢通，加上擬議的支出約束，使投資人可以接受較大赤字。新增授權將擴大硬通貨籌資選項與未來再融資曝險，但並未被當成即時財務困境。

委內瑞拉在宣布規劃重整後不到一個月，聘請Hogan Lovells擔任法律顧問，開始處理自2017年違約、估計約$1,700億債務。市場期待與美國關係改善，已使政府債券今年上漲逾80%；2027年券在約52美分，計入累積未付利息後，隱含回收率約30%。聘請顧問推進了程序，但制裁、債權核對及回收分配仍未解決。

巴西石化公司Braskem則在7月付款前，尋求債權人支持庭外重整。取得三分之一債務持有人支持，可啟動90天暫停追償，最終計畫之後仍需多數同意。股價一度下跌6.3%，儘管債券前三個月報酬約44%，遠高於新興市場企業債指標的0.6%。這波大漲之後，擬議程序再次使資本結構與事件風險受到關注。

## 前瞻市場意涵

週三數據將有助判斷，職缺大增是否代表勞動需求更廣泛地穩定。6月3日08:15美東時間公布ADP私人就業，10:00公布ISM服務業，14:00公布褐皮書；之後是6月4日初領失業救濟金，以及6月5日08:30就業報告。市場預期ADP增加12萬人、服務業指數53.8、非農就業增加8.5萬人、失業率4.3%。若結果接近預期，就業與價格又穩健，2年期及5年期仍容易受緊縮預期影響；聘僱轉弱、服務價格降溫及初領人數上升，則會給聯準會更多等待的理由。

美國財政部$690億17週國庫券標售，6月3日11:30美東時間截止，接續13:40至14:00進行上限$20億的長天期流動性支持買回。6月4日，$750億的4週及8週券標售之後，將進行最多$125億、一個月至兩年期附息公債的現金管理買回。投標倍數、非交易商參與及交割情況，可觀察公私部門持續發債時，42天期標售呈現的平穩融資能否延續。短端殖利率上升或明顯現金壓力，將使新債更難以原有成本發行。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

A jump in US job openings checked Tuesday's Treasury rally, leaving the 2-year yield unchanged even as longer bonds recovered some of Monday's losses. The 10-year yield fell 1 basis point to 4.46% and the 30-year declined 2 to 4.97%. Investors found room to buy longer maturities, but a resilient labor market and the Fed's concern over inflation kept the front end at 4.05%.

April openings rose to 7.62 million, the highest in almost two years, and layoffs fell. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said holding rates remained reasonable under uncertainty, while warning that persistent price pressure could soon require action. Swaps priced about 18 basis points of tightening by December. Oil edged higher within Monday's range, doing little to dislodge that policy outlook.

Credit buyers were less hesitant. Blue Owl Technology Finance and a CoreWeave-linked data-center borrower enlarged their bond sales and improved pricing from initial discussions. Semiconductor shares surged 5.87%, helping risk assets advance alongside long Treasuries. Abroad, a strong Japanese auction and buyers attracted by high gilt yields cushioned bond markets despite mounting expectations of tighter central-bank policy.

## Jobs Data Check the Treasury Rally

Treasuries had traded near their best levels in a month before the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey. Available positions rose to 7.62 million from 6.89 million in March, well above the 6.87 million median forecast, while fewer layoffs suggested the labor market was stabilizing. Mixed details prevented a fresh selloff, but yields moved away from their lows as the report reduced the urgency for easier policy.

Hammack described employment as near full capacity and said the current policy rate might not be restrictive. Broad price pressure in goods and non-housing services, together with annual PCE inflation of 3.8% in April, supported her caution. Patience did not rule out an increase: swaps priced roughly 18 basis points of tightening by December and a full quarter-point by March 2027.

The curve reflected that distinction. The 2-year yield held at 4.05%, while the 5-year slipped 1 basis point to 4.17%, the 10-year fell 1 to 4.46% and the 30-year declined 2 to 4.97%. The 2s10s curve flattened 1 basis point to 41, and 2s30s narrowed 2 to 92. The 2s5s10s butterfly fell 1 basis point to -17; 2s10s30s remained at -10.

At 10 years, a 1-basis-point decline in the breakeven to 2.39% accounted for the nominal move, with the real yield unchanged at 2.07%. Farther out, real yields fell 1 basis point at 20 years to 2.48% and 2 at 30 years to 2.69%. The 5-year real yield instead rose 1 basis point to 1.65%, maintaining pressure nearer the expected policy path.

WTI rose 1.74% to $93.76 and Brent gained 1.07% to $96.00, both within Monday's ranges. Their one-month declines of about 8.0% and 11.3% left the energy shock less severe than at its peak, though prices remained high. Recent oil declines from May highs had helped take Treasury yields down roughly 10 to 20 basis points across maturities. Tuesday's small moves left investors balancing that relief against the evidence of firm labor demand.

Positioning offered no decisive push. Traders had reduced some of their most extreme bearish exposure, but surveys showed investors returning from a small outright long to neutral. Options activity continued to hedge both rallies and selloffs. Services and employment data would have considerable scope to disturb that balance.

Short-term funding was orderly. Treasury accepted about $75 billion in 42-day bills at a 3.625% high rate and a 3.28 bid-to-cover ratio, up from 2.71 previously. Indirect bidders received 63.61% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 3.62% and dealers 32.77%. The smaller six-week sale is due to settle June 4. In the absence of a when-issued comparison, the stronger cover and allocation provide the clearer evidence of demand.

Bill closing yields moved in a narrow range. Four- and eight-week coupon-equivalent yields fell 1 basis point to 3.69% and 3.70%, while the six-week rose 1 to 3.70%. The 13- and 17-week yields held at 3.71% and 3.74%, and 26- and 52-week yields each declined 1 basis point. There was little sign of a common cash squeeze behind the firm policy pricing.

The Fed's portfolio raised a longer-term supply question. Economists Christina and David Romer argued that substantially shrinking the $6.7 trillion balance sheet would bring major costs without meaningful benefits, although limited changes could pass a cost-benefit test. Almost $4.5 trillion was in Treasuries and nearly $2 trillion in mortgage securities. They found the MBS concentration harder to justify, but estimated that runoff at the pace in place since 2024 would take more than a decade. A faster reduction under Chair Kevin Warsh would affect reserves, mortgage-bond supply and the amount of duration left with private investors.

Equities gained as bonds recovered. The S&P 500 rose 0.13%, the Nasdaq 100 0.48% and semiconductors 5.87%; the VIX fell 1.74% to 15.77. The AI-led advance kept prospective capital spending and debt issuance in view, even though current Treasury trading remained dominated by energy and the Fed. The dollar index edged up 0.02% to 99.22 and gold rose 0.31% to $4,489.10, with little additional dollar pressure on external borrowers and continued demand for geopolitical protection.

## Credit Buyers Back Refinancing and Contracted Revenue

Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp. sold $500 million of bonds, up from an initial $300 million target, at 265 basis points over Treasuries. The spread tightened from discussion around 300 basis points. The private-credit business-development company's notes carried an expected BBB- rating from Fitch, with proceeds earmarked for repaying existing debt.

The sale followed a roughly 5% reduction in the value of the fund's assets during the previous quarter. Blue Owl had become more cautious about software lending, although the fund maintained its dividend. Buyers were willing to fund a refinancing at the bottom of investment grade despite those portfolio concerns, extending the previous session's evidence of access for business-development companies.

UBS raised $1.5 billion of dollar Additional Tier 1 capital at a 6.875% yield. Guidance had started near 7.5% before tightening to 7.25%-7.375%, and the securities are first callable in late 2032. It was the bank's first AT1 sale since Switzerland paused proposed changes to rules on coupon capacity and replacement. Reduced regulatory uncertainty helped demand, while the long call and subordinated structure left investors exposed to extension and loss-absorption risk.

Elk Grove Village Property completed the data-center financing marketed on Monday. The indirect Prime Data Centers subsidiary increased its offer by $50 million to $900 million, pricing five-year bonds at par to yield 7.5%, the low end of discussion. Its Chicago-area facility is entirely leased to CoreWeave for 15 years, representing about $2.2 billion in contracted revenue. That lease supported the sale, with construction, a single tenant and the speculative-grade counterparty still central to the credit.

Data-center businesses had raised more than $27 billion through riskier bonds during the year, while technology companies' broader bond sales exceeded $300 billion. Successful execution showed buyers distinguishing among the financing structures. The larger supply still adds to private-sector borrowing competing with sovereign debt over time.

Listed credit funds were nearly flat: LQD slipped 0.01%, HYG rose 0.08% and JNK gained 0.04%. Those small moves sat alongside much more substantial activity in refinancing, bank capital and new infrastructure debt.

South Korean companies were changing maturities to manage higher costs. Short-term bonds and commercial-paper issuance reached 741.4 trillion won through April, up 47.1% from a year earlier, while corporate-bond issuance fell 34.1%. The 3-year AA nonguaranteed corporate yield had risen almost 100 basis points to 4.4%, compared with 3.06% on three-month commercial paper. Shortening liabilities reduced the immediate interest bill but left borrowers more exposed to future rollovers.

US municipal borrowers were expanding prepaid-energy financing. The California Community Choice Financing Authority approved up to $1.25 billion of bonds to acquire discounted long-term electricity for Pioneer Community Energy, with Goldman Sachs underwriting. In these structures, a bank or insurer receives and invests the proceeds and makes payments to procure energy; the utility's energy payments support repayment to bondholders. Investors generally receive more yield than on similarly rated municipal debt.

The segment had issued $14.6 billion during the year, up 94% from the comparable 2025 period, extending annual records set since 2022. Separately, Bank of America was slated to receive funding from Black Belt Energy Gas District's $1.15 billion prepaid-gas bond. The structures broaden public-power financing, with intermediary credit, energy contracts and payment mechanics determining the risks behind the additional yield.

Acquisition financing was also approaching the market. Banks prepared $2.5 billion of leveraged loans and high-yield bonds, plus a $250 million revolver, for Long Lake Management's roughly $6.3 billion cash purchase of American Express Global Business Travel. The package would bring new acquisition leverage to a speculative-grade market where M&A financing had been slower than expected and opportunistic loan repricing had dominated. The final instrument mix and pricing remained to be established.

Britain's transaction pipeline was quieter. Official figures showed completed domestic, inward and outward acquisitions falling to 352 in Q1 from 495, with inward deal value dropping to £14.2 billion from £33.0 billion. Fewer acquisitions could reduce bridge and permanent financing needs in sterling credit, contrasting with active US refinancing and AI-related issuance.

## High Yields Draw Buyers Despite Hawkish Central Banks

Euro-area inflation accelerated across several measures in May: headline prices rose 3.2% from a year earlier, up from 3.0%, while core inflation reached 2.5% and services 3.5%. The breadth reinforced expectations of an ECB increase on June 11, even as regional business activity contracted at its fastest pace since 2023.

Gediminas Simkus called for timely action to prevent inflation accelerating, while Olli Rehn said expectations remained anchored but action was still necessary. An initial increase aimed at protecting credibility need not imply a long tightening cycle. Persistent services pass-through, however, would strengthen the case for further moves and keep pressure on the returns investors require from longer bonds.

BOE policymaker Megan Greene said a near-term increase could be needed as the Iran conflict prolonged energy pass-through. Money markets fully priced a quarter-point rise by September and an 85% chance of another by year-end. Governor Andrew Bailey argued that officials had some time, citing already tighter financial conditions and fragile demand.

High yields were nevertheless attracting gilt buyers. Insight Investment, with $836 billion under management, had been adding longer-dated UK bonds as forward yields reached around or above 6%. Thirty-year gilts yielded more than 5.5%, the highest among a group of 21 developed markets. At those valuations, investors could find compensation for inflation and fiscal risk without assuming the BOE was finished tightening.

Japan's auction produced a more immediate rally. The 10-year JGB yield fell 11 basis points to 2.57% after a 3.53 bid-to-cover ratio, above the 3.35 average over the preceding 12 months. Yields at their highest since 1996 had made the bonds look cheap, and improving long-end sentiment brought buyers back. Yet OIS still assigned roughly a 76% chance to a BOJ move that month, and the yen was approaching 160 per dollar.

China's central bank was instead trying to restrain an overly rapid decline in yields. The PBOC conducted just 200 million yuan of seven-day reverse repos, its smallest daily operation on record, against excess liquidity and weak loan growth. The 10-year government yield had finished Monday at 1.70%, its lowest since August, before long-bond futures slipped. The low yield level remained a reminder of China's weaker growth and credit-demand setting.

After the New York close, reporting on Asia emphasized the combination of oil-driven cost pressure and AI-related demand. Government yields had risen, while the Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah weakened as import bills and external balances came under strain. In Japan, five of the nine BOJ board members had recently signaled support for further normalization, potentially giving Governor Kazuo Ueda a majority. The regional developments added to the policy questions awaiting the next session.

Poland offered a different inflation outcome. Its central bank held the key rate at 3.75% for a third month after May inflation slowed to 3.1% from 3.2%, below a 3.6% median forecast. Officials still cited energy, loose fiscal policy, wages and fuel regulation as risks. Softer actual inflation allowed a pause even as euro-area and UK policymakers leaned toward tightening.

## Fiscal Credibility Separates Sovereign Borrowers

Emerging-market dollar debt gained, with EMB rising 0.26% and the dollar broadly stable. The aggregate move concealed a much wider gap between countries strengthening public finances and borrowers approaching restructuring.

South Africa's primary surplus reached 1.1% of GDP in the year through March, above Treasury's 0.9% forecast. The main-budget deficit was 4.3%, better than the 4.6% estimate. Officials said debt had stabilized after peaking near 78.9% of GDP and was projected to fall toward 68.3% by 2033-34. Better revenue, lower spending and reduced debt-service costs supported the case for future rating upgrades despite the common energy shock.

Senegal's political dispute was intensifying its financing problem. A cabinet conflict between President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko added to fiscal uncertainty. The 2031 dollar bond traded around 54 cents, down from a mid-February peak of 68, and sovereign spreads exceeded 1,500 basis points over Treasuries. Its three dollar notes had lost 2.5% during the year, against a 1.5% gain in a broader EM dollar-bond index.

Investors expected $92.5 million of coupon payments due that month to be made, but regional-market repayments of CFA 296 billion, about $524 million, added to the cash requirement. With the IMF's $1.8 billion program suspended after hidden obligations were discovered, paying the immediate coupons would not resolve access to larger financing. Expectations of a broader restructuring were growing.

Chile sought more borrowing authority from a stronger position. President Jose Antonio Kast's government asked Congress for an additional $6.2 billion on top of the $17.4 billion already authorized, having raised more than $8 billion during the year. It had revised the deficit forecast to 2.4% of GDP from the previous administration's 1.8% and could issue as much as $6 billion in foreign currency.

Sovereign yields nevertheless edged lower and default-protection costs fell to their lowest since mid-February. Continuing market access and proposed expenditure restraint helped investors accommodate the larger deficit. The request would expand hard-currency borrowing options and future refinancing exposure, without being treated as an immediate distress event.

Venezuela took a procedural step toward restructuring, appointing Hogan Lovells as legal counsel less than a month after announcing plans to rework about $170 billion of debt in default since 2017. Government bonds had already gained more than 80% during the year on expectations of US rapprochement. The 2027 notes traded near 52 cents, implying roughly 30% recovery after accrued unpaid interest. Appointing counsel advanced the process, with sanctions, claim reconciliation and recovery allocation still unresolved.

Brazil's Braskem sought creditor support for an out-of-court restructuring before July payments. Holders of one-third of the debt could enable a 90-day standstill, followed by the majority approval required for a final plan. Shares fell as much as 6.3%, even though the petrochemicals company's bonds had returned about 44% over three months, against 0.6% for an EM corporate gauge. The proposed process brought capital-structure and event risks back into focus after that rally.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday's releases will help determine whether the jump in openings reflects a broader stabilization in labor demand. ADP private payrolls are due June 3 at 08:15 ET, ISM services at 10:00 ET and the Beige Book at 14:00 ET, followed by claims on June 4 and the employment report on June 5 at 08:30 ET. Consensus is 120,000 for ADP, 53.8 for services, 85,000 for payrolls and 4.3% for unemployment. Firm employment and prices alongside those readings would leave the 2- and 5-year sectors sensitive to tightening expectations. Weaker hiring, softer service prices and rising claims would give the Fed more reason to wait.

Treasury's $69 billion 17-week bill auction closes June 3 at 11:30 ET, followed by a long-duration liquidity-support buyback capped at $2 billion from 13:40 to 14:00 ET. On June 4, the $75 billion 4- and 8-week auctions precede a cash-management buyback of up to $12.5 billion in one-month to two-year coupons. Cover, nondealer participation and settlement will show whether the calm funding conditions evident in the 42-day sale persist as public and private issuance continues. A rise in short yields or visible cash pressure would make new debt more expensive to place.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda speaks June 3, the RBI decides June 5 and the ECB meets June 11. Sustained crude declines, firmer energy-importer currencies and signs of contained pass-through would allow more patient guidance. Renewed disruption, weaker Asian currencies or ECB language pointing beyond an initial increase would instead raise the risk of more synchronized tightening, keeping pressure on inflation compensation and oil-importer refinancing even if US growth remains resilient.

section_summaries.summary: A large increase in job openings kept short Treasury yields steady as longer bonds gained. Corporate deals drew strong demand, equities advanced and high overseas yields attracted buyers despite hawkish policy signals.

section_summaries.summary: Blue Owl, UBS and a CoreWeave-linked borrower improved deal terms. Korean companies shortened funding, municipal prepaid-energy issuance expanded, and new acquisition finance approached a market still dominated by refinancing.

section_summaries.section_title: High Yields Draw Buyers Despite Hawkish Central Banks
section_summaries.summary: Broader euro-area inflation and BOE debate kept tightening in view. Gilt valuations and a strong Japanese auction drew buyers nevertheless, while China and Poland presented softer demand or inflation outcomes.

South Africa improved its budget and Chile sought more debt authorization without a distressed market reaction. Senegal faced growing repayment and political strain; Venezuela and Braskem took steps toward restructuring.

ADP, ISM services and payrolls will test labor stabilization. Bill auctions and buybacks will show whether funding remains calm, while Asian and European policy signals will clarify the response to elevated energy costs.
